help.tips[0].examples[0].en: After a meeting lasting more than nine hours, the supervisory board of Brenner Maschinenbau AG carried out a change of course in the night to Thursday that industry insiders considered unthinkable only a few weeks ago.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: On the works council the plan meets with fierce resistance.
help.tips[0].examples[2].en: The works council would exhaust every legal means to tie the sale at least to binding site guarantees.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: Berufung, like Einspruch, is eingelegt. Bedenken are angemeldet and a Kurswechsel is vollzogen: each noun has its own verb.
help.tips[0].en.text: In business German the noun dictates its partner, and a near-synonym sounds wrong: a Kurswechsel is vollzogen (not erledigt or verrichtet), losses are herb, resistance is something a plan stößt auf, Bedenken are angemeldet (Einspruch is eingelegt – a different collocation), legal means are ausgeschöpft, and a decision stellt die Weichen. Learn the pair, not the single word.
help.tips[0].en.title: The noun chooses its verb or adjective
help.tips[0].en.trap: Bedenken äußern is also correct German, but the text asks for the participle that goes with hatte … Bedenken: angemeldet. Einspruch einlegen does not transfer to Bedenken.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The changeover would be painful for everyone involved, but there was no alternative.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Whoever hesitates today loses touch with the competition from Asia tomorrow.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: The second sentence still reports the CFO, so it stays in the Konjunktiv I. ist would make the forecast the newspaper's own.
help.tips[1].en.text: Once the reporter names a speaker (räumte ein, sagte Ortmann, erklärte Albers), every following clause that reports that speaker stays in the Konjunktiv I, even without a new verb of saying: habe, sei, werde, könne, wolle, müsse, zögere, verliere. The indicative returns only where the journalist speaks in their own voice (Die Anteilseigner zeigten sich … unbeeindruckt; Ob der Neuanfang gelingt, dürfte sich … zeigen).
help.tips[1].en.title: Konjunktiv I carries the whole reported passage
help.tips[1].en.trap: Do not switch to wird or kann mid-report: the indicative would make the claim the newspaper’s own.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: The roughly 2,300 employees of the division had voluntarily gone without pay rises during the crisis years, Ortmann said in the morning outside the factory gate in Heilbronn.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: CEO Martin Kessler admitted to journalists that the company had underestimated the weak demand in South America for too long and had taken countermeasures too late.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: In the plural the Konjunktiv I haben looks like the indicative, so the press uses hätten. hatten is the plain past and reports nothing.
help.tips[2].en.text: In the plural the Konjunktiv I of haben is haben – identical to the indicative, so it cannot signal reported speech. The press then uses the Konjunktiv II hätten as a stand-in. In the singular the distinct form habe is used, so hätte is not needed there.
help.tips[2].en.title: hätten when Konjunktiv I looks like the indicative
help.tips[2].en.trap: hatten (no umlaut) is the plain past indicative and reports nothing.
help.hookEn: Read German business news like an insider: the fixed word pairs of the financial pages, and who is really making each claim.
help.introEn: A business-press report of about 420 words on a supervisory board meeting at a fictional engineering group, Brenner Maschinenbau AG, with twelve gaps. Two things make the register, and the gaps test both. First, fixed collocations of the business pages: einen Kurswechsel vollziehen, herbe Einbußen, auf erbitterten Widerstand stoßen, Bedenken anmelden, alle rechtlichen Mittel ausschöpfen, die Weichen stellen. Second, the journalistic Konjunktiv I, sustained over whole reported passages once a speaker is named: the CEO (man habe … unterschätzt, sie sei jedoch ohne Alternative), the works council chair (Die rund 2300 Beschäftigten der Sparte hätten …, Zum Dank wolle man sie nun …) and the board chairman (Wer heute zögere, verliere morgen den Anschluss). Collocation gaps give the English; Konjunktiv gaps give the infinitive. Read each paragraph once for who is speaking before you fill it in.
help.rememberEn[0]: Kurswechsel vollziehen, herbe Einbußen, auf Widerstand stoßen, Bedenken anmelden, Mittel ausschöpfen, die Weichen stellen.
help.rememberEn[1]: A named speaker → Konjunktiv I for the whole report (habe, sei, werde, könne, wolle); plural haben → hätten.
